topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, frames the course of cancer lectures, and outlines the learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Mechanisms and drivers of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological fundamentals of cancer as a genetic and evolutionary disease driven by an interplay of endogenous processes, bad luck, and environmental exposures.

topics.label: Epidemiological patterns and environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss epidemiological geographic variations in cancer rates and examine specific environmental, infectious, and chemical agents that induce malignancy.

topics.label: Initiation, promotion, and host susceptibility factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the mechanistic distinction between cancer initiators and promoters, including inflammation and host developmental vulnerability.

topics.label: Mid-lecture summary of carcinogenesis mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides a self-contained summary of the preceding discussion on direct mutagens, promoters, and host-specific factors.

topics.label: Methods for detecting and testing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine experimental, mutational, and epidemiological methodologies used to identify and prove the carcinogenicity of substances.

topics.label: Conclusion and risk-benefit analysis
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by framing carcinogenic exposure within daily risk-benefit decisions and summarising core takeaways.
